ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended per Ley 6/2023, de 7 de julio (BOE 8 Jul 2023), transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil); Real Decreto-ley 19/2018, de 23 de noviembre, de servicios de pago; relevant Bank of Spain Circulars; Spanish UBO Register (Registro de Titularidades Reales) administered by the Registro Mercantil Central for notarial filing transparency.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of No Prior Registration of Company Name (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Mercantil Central / Ministry of Justice (Madrid)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic administrative certificate, no Apostille required for incorporation before a Spanish notary; Apostille required only if used abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución de Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) including articles of association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Directing Spanish Notary (Notario autorizante within chosen local jurisdiction)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial registration in the Registro Mercantil; Apostille obtainable via the Colegio Notarial only when the deed must be produced to foreign authorities (e.g., foreign bank due diligence)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Spanish Bank Capital Deposit Certificate (Certificado de Depósito Bancario del Capital Social)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish authorized credit institution holding the restricted capital deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic bank-issued instrument, no Apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign Criminal Record Certificate of each appointed director, legal representative and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal records authority of the country of origin (e.g., National Police, Home Office, FBI, Ministry of Justice)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for states not party to the 1961 Apostille Convention) plus sworn Spanish translation by an officially authorized translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign Birth Certificate / Valid Passport copy / Proof of Address of individual shareholders and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil Registry or competent authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization where the Apostille Convention does not apply) plus sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney executed by non-resident shareholders in favor of the founding Spanish representative (if incorporation is carried out by attorney-in-fact)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin, duly legalized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (as applicable per origin state) plus sworn Spanish translation and, where deemed necessary, certification of a representative appointed before the Consular Section of the Embassy of Spain

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: NIE Certificate (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) for each foreign director, shareholder and UBO obtaining pre-incorporation clearance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish National Police (Cuerpo Nacional de Policía, Oficina de Extranjería) / unified DGSJFP administrative scheme
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Spanish administrative certificate, no Apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory and continuous screening of all directors, UBOs, signatories, and beneficial intermediaries against the consolidated European Union restrictive measures list (Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and amendments), the UN Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC SDN list (essential for USD-cleared remittance rails), SEPBLAC financial intelligence indicators, the national police and judicial proscription lists, and FATF public statements. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is statutorily required for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP) as defined by Directive (EU) 2015/849 Article 3(9) and Spanish implementing law; re-screening occurs at least every six months and immediately upon any trigger event (new PEP status, change of control, adverse media, or correspondent banking change). Compliance evidence — including screen shots, identity documents, and risk files — must be retained for a minimum of 10 years per Article 25 Ley 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central - Sistema de Despacho Electrónico de Certificaciones / Denominaciones Sociales (https://www.rmc.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be lawful, distinctive, and presentable in Spanish (Castilian) alphabet form; foreign expressions are admissible only if transliterated into the Spanish alphabet without graphic ambiguities and merged with the legal corporate type suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.'; the name cannot be identical or misleadingly similar to any pre-existing denomination recorded in the RMC, nor may it imply a public entity, regulate an activity not actually pursued, or contain foreign script without an authentic Spanish transliteration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Mercantil Central issues a negative resolution (denegación) or prevents registration on the basis of identity, resemblance, or prohibition, the applicant may: (i) file written representations and amended denomination requests through the RMC system; (ii) lodge a recurso de alzada before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month of formal notification, accompanied by a memorandum distinguishing the proposed name from conflicting denominations; (iii) alternatively, after exhaustion or directly where appropriate, challenge the administrative act before the Juzgado Central Contencioso-Administrativo / Audiencia Nacional within two months. In parallel, the applicant should immediately reserve two or three alternative names in order of preference, as issuance of a fresh certificación negativa is a mandatory prerequisite to executing the notarial deed. No ministerial fee is charged for the appeal, but professional representation at prevailing market rates is customary.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an SL incorporated under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital, Article 9 requires the registered office (domicilio social) to be situated in Spanish territory at the place where the effective and actual administration/management is located or where the principal establishment or main operations are based; a pure virtual address without local management presence will not satisfy Bank of Spain or SEPBLAC substance requirements for an ISIC 6619 payment/remittance business. Virtual offices are tolerated only as supplementary administrative/mailing addresses, provided the physical registered office is a real accessible location where books and minimum substance (staff, IT infrastructure, compliance records) are demonstrable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 90% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by SEPBLAC / Bank of Spain within the first 18 months of authorized operation, and a near-certainty (statistically 100%) during the first renewal or filing cycle, given the mandated high-risk tier for money remittance services under Spain's AML/CFT and payment institution supervision framework; unannounced inspections by the Tax Agency (AEAT) and Social Security Inspectorate are also independently likely.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificación negativa de denominación social (negative name certificate request and issuance including online portal fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Ministry of Justice, Madrid)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed tariff per Reglamento del Registro Mercantil; approximately EUR 19 (USD 21) for online application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fee for escritura de constitución de SL (notarial deed of incorporation, including statutory model bylaws, Article 22 LSC documentation and related notarial copies)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Directing Spanish Notary (Notaría del lugar del domicilio social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial arancel (Arancel Notarial) computed on subscribed share capital bracket and deed length; EUR 3,000 SL capital bracket, market range EUR 420–EUR 650

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First inscription fee at the provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil de la provincia del domicilio), plus related certified registry copies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Valencia)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry fee scale under Real Decreto 1497/1991 as updated; approximate market cost EUR 150 for standard SL first filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) processing fee for each non-resident director/UBO, including police appointment and administrative tax
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish National Police / Oficina de Extranjería (through Tasa 790-026)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory national tax of approximately EUR 10.50 plus administrative service fees; representative market cost EUR 50–EUR 60 per person

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostilles, sworn legal translations, and consular legalization of foreign personal documents (criminal record certificates, birth certificates, POA, passport copies) for each foreign shareholder/director/UBO
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign authorities (e.g., Secretary of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Notary Public) and Spanish traductor jurado
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention statutory rates for apostilles, plus market benchmark for sworn translation EUR 80–EUR 200 per document batch

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stage 1 pre-incorporation legal package: corporate due diligence, UBO piercing report, AML/CFT institutional design, PEP/sanctions screening, drafting of ancillary declarations, advice on payment institution licensing under Real Decreto-ley 19/2018
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained external law firm (member of a Spanish Bar; Madrid/Valencia/Málaga)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark prevailing hourly rates for cross-border Spanish incorporations; typical fixed-fee range EUR 900–EUR 1,200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of Spanish bank capital deposit account and issuance of the statutory certificate (Certificado de depósito bancario) for the EUR 3,000 minimum share capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish credit institution (e.g., Banco Santander, BBVA, Sabadell, or CaixaBank)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing bank market tariff; no ministerial fee; some banks waive the charge for business packages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LEI (Legal Entity Identifier) preliminary registration and ELF code preparation to be activated immediately post-incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: GLEIF-accredited Local Operating Unit (e.g., Informa D&B S.A.U. or Bolsa de Madrid certification desk)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: GLEIF market benchmark for standard registration, EUR 100–EUR 150

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial transmittal within first inscription fee; external compliance advisory at market benchmark EUR 130

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), including Articles 4, 20-23, 62, 78-79, 160, 209-252, and 253-273; Law 14/2013 on entrepreneurs and electronic incorporation procedures; Royal Legislative Decree 19/2018 on payment services and payment institutions, including Articles 2, 5, 11, 12, 15-18, and 22-29; Royal Decree 736/2019 implementing payment-service authorization and supervision rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) under the Directorate-General for Legal Certainty and Public Faith (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública), Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), followed by registration of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The corporate minimum capital of an SL is EUR 1.00 under Article 4 of the Companies Act. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and shareholders have subsidiary liability for the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital upon liquidation. There is no general statutory escrow requirement. A bank certificate evidencing monetary contributions may be provided; for an SL, founders may instead state in the deed that they are jointly liable for the reality of the contributions. A payment institution authorized exclusively for money remittance must separately satisfy the regulatory initial capital requirement of EUR 20,000 under Royal Legislative Decree 19/2018 and maintain funds and own resources in accordance with Banco de España requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts the subscription and payment of its entire issued share capital as recorded in the incorporation deed and shareholders’ register; (2) the registered office is adopted at [full Spanish address], with authority granted to update the address within Spain where legally permitted; (3) [name] is appointed Managing Director and [name] is appointed Secretary, each accepting office and agreeing to comply with applicable law, the articles, payment-services regulation, AML obligations, and Banco de España requirements; and (4) the officers are authorized to complete all registry, tax, banking, licensing, and publication formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), electronic name-certification service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application for a negative certificate of company name, listing up to five proposed names in priority order. Ensure the name is distinguishable and includes the legal form or its abbreviation. Obtain the certificate before execution of the incorporation deed and preserve the original or electronically verifiable certificate for the notary.
required_dossiers: Proposed legal form: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, submit an alternative name or amend the proposed name. If the certificate contains an error, request correction from the Central Mercantile Registry before signing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification and Identify Foreign Participants
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria), including its electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain NIE numbers for non-Spanish individual directors or shareholders and NIF numbers for foreign corporate shareholders where required. Apply for the provisional company NIF using Form 036 and submit the incorporation documentation or proposed deed information. Foreign documents must be apostilled or legalized and accompanied by sworn Spanish translations unless an applicable exemption applies.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate registry extract, constitutional documents, and certificate of authority
Apostille or legalization and sworn Spanish translation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to an Agencia Tributaria information request through the electronic register or appointed representative. Correct identification inconsistencies and resubmit Form 036 with the missing evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute the Public Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary Public (notario), with electronic transmission through the CIRCE or notarial filing system where used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the notary with the name certificate, articles of association, shareholder and director identification, registered-office evidence, beneficial-owner information, and capital-contribution evidence or the statutory founder declaration. Execute the deed in Spanish or through an authorized interpreter. The deed must state the company name, purpose, registered office, capital, shares, management structure, and shareholder allocations.
required_dossiers: Registered-office title, lease, or owner authorization
Bank certificate for capital contributions or statutory founder liability declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure notarial objections by supplying missing documents, correcting the articles, or executing a rectifying deed. Do not submit an incomplete deed to the Mercantile Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronically signed public deed, provisional NIF evidence, name certificate, and applicable Registry forms through the notary or the Registry electronic portal. Pay the variable notarial and Registry tariffs. Obtain the Registry entry, definitive NIF, and electronic company certification. File the deed promptly after execution to preserve priority and avoid expiration of the name certificate.
required_dossiers: Registry application and tariff payment evidence
Director acceptance statements, where separately required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a defect note, obtain the written qualification, cure each defect by supplementary filing or rectifying deed, and resubmit within the applicable priority period. Appeal or seek governmental review where a defect is legally disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Social Security, and Beneficial-Ownership Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency, General Treasury of Social Security (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social), and the applicable Beneficial Ownership Registry systems
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Replace the provisional NIF with the definitive NIF, register the applicable business activity through Form 036, and obtain an electronic certificate for the company. Register directors or employees with Social Security before activity begins. Maintain current beneficial-owner information and file required corporate, accounting, and tax books through the Mercantile Registry electronic platform.
required_dossiers: Director and employee Social Security data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected electronic filings, submit missing forms through the electronic register, and request administrative rectification. Late registrations may trigger penalties or require voluntary disclosure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco de España, Department of Authorization and Registration of Payment Institutions and Electronic Money Institutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before providing remittance services, submit an authorization application under Royal Legislative Decree 19/2018 and Royal Decree 736/2019. The dossier must demonstrate EUR 20,000 initial capital for exclusive money-remittance activity, governance suitability, qualifying holdings, business plan, safeguarding arrangements, internal controls, AML/CFT framework, complaints handling, ICT and security controls, outsourcing arrangements, operational resilience, and fit-and-proper management. Do not market or execute regulated remittances before authorization and registration.
required_dossiers: Business plan and three-year financial projections
Evidence of initial capital and own funds
Governance chart and director fit-and-proper evidence
ICT, cybersecurity, incident-reporting, and business-continuity policies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond within the Banco de España deadline to clarification requests and cure deficiencies through the electronic application file. A refusal may be challenged through the applicable administrative appeal and judicial review procedures; the applicant must not commence regulated activity pending final authorization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Agents and Implement AML and Operational Controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco de España for payment agents and the Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Offences (SEPBLAC) for AML supervision and reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before appointing cash-pickup or other agents, submit the required agent information to Banco de España and conduct documented due diligence, training, monitoring, and reconciliation. Register as an obligated entity for AML purposes where required, appoint a compliance representative, implement customer due diligence, sanctions screening, suspicious-transaction reporting, record retention, and cash-control procedures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Suspend the affected agent or service channel, correct the filing, and provide Banco de España or SEPBLAC with remediation evidence. Material AML or safeguarding failures require immediate escalation and documented corrective action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Premises and Workplace Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Ayuntamiento responsible for the premises, with the competent regional occupational-risk and fire-safety authorities where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the premises require a responsible declaration, prior activity communication, opening license, works permit, accessibility certificate, or technical project. File the applicable municipal form before opening. Ensure fire detection, emergency exits, electrical safety, accessibility, occupational-risk prevention, and cash-handling controls are documented. A purely administrative office normally does not require an industrial operating permit or environmental authorization.
required_dossiers: Electrical and structural certificates, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure municipal technical objections, submit amended plans or certificates, and request inspection or reconsideration. Do not occupy or operate a regulated premises before the applicable declaration, license, or inspection requirement is satisfied.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Banco de España for authorization as a payment institution and supervision of money-remittance services; the competent Autonomous Community industrial authority applies only to premises, electrical, fire, or technical installations where triggered. No manufacturing or industrial production license is ordinarily required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Authorization as a Payment Institution to Provide Money Remittance Services (autorización como entidad de pago para prestar el servicio de envío de dinero), with Banco de España registration before commencement of regulated activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge and the competent environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt or not applicable for an administrative remittance office, cash-pickup point, or digital payment operation without construction, industrial emissions, significant wastewater, or hazardous-material handling. A project-specific screening is required if substantial premises works or a listed activity is introduced.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or industrial VOC emissions are expected. Ordinary municipal waste must be separated and managed through authorized channels. Electronic equipment, batteries, confidential paper, cash-transport materials, and any hazardous waste must be transferred to authorized waste managers under applicable Spanish and Autonomous Community waste rules. Any discharge, generator, fuel storage, or construction activity must comply with the relevant municipal, water, air-quality, and waste permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain the applicable municipal opening, activity, or responsible-declaration filing; maintain fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, evacuation routes, alarms, signage, and an emergency plan. Obtain structural, electrical, accessibility, and fire-system certificates where required by the premises or activity. Complete an occupational-risk assessment, worker information and training, health-and-safety coordination, and cash-handling security assessment. Cash-pickup premises may require additional municipal security, accessibility, and opening-hour controls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); taxpayer portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation, the Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) must apply for a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) using Form 036/037 at the local AEAT office immediately after execution of the public deed and inscription in the Registro Mercantil. The definitive NIF is issued after verification of the deed and economic activity. For foreign entities establishing a branch or permanent establishment in Spain, a NIF for the Spanish PE is obtained via Form 036 and requires appointment of a Spanish fiscal representative. A non-resident entity without a PE but having Spanish tax obligations (e.g., VAT from distance sales or Spanish source income) must obtain a non-resident NIF (NIF-ES) through Form 030/036 with an NIE (identificación de extranjero) for the legal representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no check-the-box election; the SL is a fully taxable Spanish resident entity subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on worldwide income. Available elections include voluntary VAT grouping (Grupo de IVA) under the Spanish VAT Law, option for joint taxation in consolidated tax groups under Articles 55–75 of the Corporate Income Tax Law (LIS), and designation under the ETVE foreign holding company regime for eligible entities. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; Spain has implemented EU Directive ATAD with mandatory rules neutralizing such mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish Value Added Tax, harmonised under EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary registration threshold; any person carrying out taxable economic activities in Spain must register for IVA before commencing activity. For intra-Community distance sales of goods, the Union-wide threshold of EUR 10,000 per calendar year applies, above which Spanish VAT is chargeable. A non-established foreign business has no threshold and must register immediately before conducting any taxable supply in Spain.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates B2B electronic invoicing under Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and Royal Decree 1007/2023, requiring structured formats such as Facturae. The SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) compulsory scheme applies to taxpayers exceeding EUR 8,000,000 turnover and VAT groups, requiring near real-time electronic transmission of invoicing records to AEAT within four business days (extended to eight days for received invoices). The Verifactu regulation obliges certified billing software to generate hashed, non-editable records with QR transmission for fiscal control; there is no continuous transaction control stamping, but clearance is achieved through mandatory electronic filing and real-time reporting.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to third countries are zero-rated when the goods are physically removed from the EU and the seller retains proof of export, including a customs export declaration (DUA) and transport documents. For cross-border remittance services, the financial intermediate services are generally exempt from IVA (not zero-rated) under Article 20.Uno.18º LIVA; for services consumed outside the EU, the place of supply may fall outside Spain under Article 69 LIVA, resulting in non-subjection rather than a zero-rating claim. Claims to zero-rating require robust documentation of the B2B status of the recipient, its non-EU location, and actual service provision.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Documento Único Administrativo – DUA)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill/CMR haulage document)
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de liquidación de ingresos)
SWIFT MT103/payment rail confirmation evidencing settlement
Commercial invoice and contract evidencing service recipient outside Spain
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False, inaccurate, or artificially delayed export declarations may trigger AEAT audits with retrospective VAT assessment, denial of zero-rating, and clawback of input VAT credited. Infractions are penalised under Articles 191–194 of the General Tax Law (LGT); material fraud involving amounts exceeding EUR 120,000 activates criminal fiscal liability under Articles 305 and 308 of the Spanish Criminal Code (Law 10/1995). Late payment interest applies from the due date, and penalties range from 50% of the evaded amount up to 150% for intentional concealment. Recurrent abuses in the remittance sector also expose the licensed payment institution to regulatory enforcement by Banco de España and Sepblac, including suspension of licence and personal liability of compliance officers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the national competent authority, in coordination with the Eurosystem/European Central Bank for monetary and FX policy; foreign investment filings are processed through the Ministry of Economy and the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Spain for both current and capital account transactions under EU Treaty of Lisbon Article 63 TFEU. No exchange controls apply to non-residents or residents. Dividend and profit remittances are unrestricted after demonstrating compliance with corporate accounting rules and 19% non-resident income tax withholding (reduced by tax treaty if applicable). No prior Banco de España authorization is required for normal treasury flows, but all cross-border transactions require statistical declaration via the receiving financial institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds. Both resident and non-resident entities may retain foreign currency in authorised accounts. Cross-border payments exceeding EUR 10,000 and all foreign-currency transactions must be reported through the designated bank as part of Spain's balance-of-payments statistics; no minimum holding period or forced liquidation applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Multi-Currency) and Safeguarded Funds Account for Remittance Settlement
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Capital Escrow Account / Liquidity Clearing EUR Account
Operational Account and Cash Pickup Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for EEA-regulated e-money institutions (EMIs) exercising passporting rights under PSD2 after filing with Banco de España; low and generally not viable for non-EEA offshore EMIs, which cannot lawfully maintain treasury accounts or provide payment services without a local branch or a Spanish-authorised agent. Cross-border digital EMIs may be used as clearance partners only after their EU/EEA passport status has been evidenced in the Spanish register.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one director and the appointed AML compliance officer must attend an in-person KYC interview at a Spanish branch or bank headquarters before onboarding approval. Remote opening is not accepted for this high-risk ISIC 6619 entity unless a Banco de España-certified video identity platform is used and a parallel in-person appointment is arranged for the responsible securities/compliance director. All non-resident directors absent from the interview must submit apostilled copies of passports, power-of-attorney documentation, and a notarised sworn statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company purpose is cross-border remittance (correspondent cash pickup + SWIFT) which is categorised as high-risk under Banco de España AML regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full AML/CFT manual, corporate criminal risk assessment, business-plan narrative of exactly how outgoing remittances are funded, surveillance and transaction-monitoring system description, UBO identification package, source-of-funds evidence on the initial injected share capital, and a copy of the pending or granted payment-institution licence application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholders are located in Latin American jurisdictions with perceived elevated money-laundering or political risk, creating red flags on UBO legitimacy and reputational risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passport copies and sworn source-of-wealth declaration for each UBO; notarial certificate of good standing in the resident jurisdiction; tax residence certificates for the last 3 years; letters of reference from a front-line bank in that jurisdiction; and a detailed explanation of the economic channel, using independent remittance market rate benchmarks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SL with no audited accounts and limited operating history, combined with a high projected daily settlement volume.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised deed of incorporation, NIF/company registration certificate from the Commercial Registry, interim-equity and liquidity forecasts, a signed financial-liquidity covenant supported by future concluded agent agreements, and a Board resolution authorising the bank to access the Banco de España financial information database to verify transaction assumptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank cannot reconcile client's request to open a separate escrow/safeguarding account without a final payment-institution licence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal acknowledgement receipt of the licence application before Banco de España, a timetabled implementation plan to secure licence approval, an independent legal opinion confirming lawful status as a licensed remittance agency, and a memorandum of understanding with a legal-entity custodian to hold funds in a segregated insurance-protected interest-bearing account during the pre-licensing phase.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Spanish SL's EUR clearing account. The remittance information field must cite the statutory purpose classification under Spain's balance-of-payments regime: foreign direct investment equity contribution (bank-assigned purpose code 'FDI-Cap' or counterpart ISO 20022 purpose 'INTC' with detailed narrative 'Aporte de capital social a SL - ESCRITURA Y NIF'). Beneficiary designation must include the SL's NIF and the company legal name. Receiving bank will verify corporate deed and shareholder identity, and for inflows over EUR 3,005,000 the operation must be reported to the Spanish Foreign Investment Registry. No exchange-control authorisation is required, but the transfer must be referenced in the bank's balance-of-payments declaration system before availability of cleared funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade and remittance disbursements include: (i) SWIFT MT103 for individual customer remittances and corporate trade payments to non-EU beneficiaries; (ii) SWIFT MT202/205 for nostro-account coverage in currencies where the Spanish bank has no direct clearing relationship; (iii) commercial letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700/MT710 when importing underlying goods from Latin American or Asian suppliers; and (iv) SEPA Credit Transfer for all settlements into EU/EEA banks. Each outbound instruction must carry the bank's purpose code for trade or remittance (e.g., 'Trade-Other' or 'Remittance') and be supported by a commercial contract, invoice, or victim-facing customer instruction to satisfy taxation and AML traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/LatAm-Cross forwards with an EU-authorised credit institution, strictly backed by existing cross-border remittance inflows
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for soft-currency baskets where the Bank of Spain maintains no published fix, subject to a bespoke ISDA wrapper and real-economy remittance exposure
Plain-vanilla FX swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL) for corridor-liquidity smoothing between the foreign correspondent pool and the Spanish operational account
Cross-currency interest rate swaps only for large infrastructure refinancings and approved by the Board under the remittance company's treasury-borrowing policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales) with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil del domicilio social (Commercial Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by the ordinary general meeting within six months after the fiscal year-end and deposited within one month after approval; for a 31-December fiscal year, approval by 30 June and deposit by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registral closure blocking all future corporate registrations until the deposit is made; director liability; late filing penalties; repeated non-compliance may trigger judicial or administrative liquidation and registry cancellation after liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the six-month period following the tax year-end; for a calendar fiscal year, by 25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5% to 20% depending on delay, plus late-payment interest and administrative penalties under the General Tax Law; continued non-payment may result in asset attachment and enforcement proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ultimate beneficial owner declaration (Declaración Anual de Titular Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil del domicilio social (Commercial Registry UBO filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually together with the deposit of annual accounts (by 31 July for a calendar-year SL); any change in shareholding or UBO must be reported within one month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML Law 10/2010 infringement regime: very serious omissions may attract fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 150,000; registral filings may also be blocked until the declaration is submitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements and audit report to the financial supervisor (licensed payment institution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Banco de España (payment institution supervisory files)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual submission within the period fixed by Banco de España circulars, generally within four months after the fiscal year-end (30 April for calendar-year filers).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Sanctions under Spanish payment services law and AML law: fines proportional to net worth or fixed amounts up to EUR 150,000; persistent breach may lead to revocation of the payment institution license.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for all licensed payment institutions regardless of size. General SL threshold under Ley de Sociedades de Capital: audit required when, for two consecutive years, the company meets at least two of (i) total assets exceed EUR 4,000,000; (ii) annual net turnover exceeds EUR 8,000,000; (iii) average workforce exceeds 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, Real Decreto 1514/2007 as amended); IFRS-EU applies to consolidated financial statements and listed entities, not to individual SL accounts unless voluntarily adopted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spanish law does not use a UK-style confirmation statement. For an SL, share transfers must be formalized in a notarial instrument where required, then recorded in the Book of Members; the transfer is effective against the company once entered. Companies must submit a UBO declaration with the annual accounts and update it within one month of any shareholding change altering beneficial ownership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (inscripción de administradores in the Commercial Registry and internal director records)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate. Qualifying newly created entities generally apply 15% in the first tax period in which they obtain a positive taxable base and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions, including entities that are asset-holding entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential incentives include the 15% rate for qualifying newly created entities, research and development and technological innovation credits, and other statutory deductions and credits. Eligibility, limits, and carryforward rules are fact-specific. No general holiday applies to remittance businesses.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward under current general rules; use is generally limited to 70% of the pre-carryforward taxable base, with a minimum offset of EUR 1 million, subject to statutory exceptions and additional restrictions. The schema's five-year figure is not Spain's general rule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, annual Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic headquarters. Modelo 202 is generally used for advance instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; advance instalments generally three times per year where required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 is due within 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual deadline is 1–25 July of the following year. Modelo 202 instalments are generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December, subject to the applicable payment and filing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the Spanish SL by tax identification number, legal name, tax domicile, tax period, and applicable filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not replace the Spanish SL as the corporate taxpayer. Use the SL's Spanish tax identification number and registered tax-period details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the accounting profit or loss and reconcile it to the taxable base through required permanent and temporary adjustments under Spanish corporate tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Spanish-company income and required related-party adjustments; do not report a shareholder's foreign income as the SL's income solely because the shareholder is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the taxable base after permitted adjustments, loss offsets, and applicable limits; disclose and track losses as required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same Spanish loss-utilisation limits to the SL regardless of shareholder residence; retain evidence supporting losses and any claimed offsets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the rate appropriate to the entity and tax period and claim only substantiated deductions, credits, and incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder's status does not itself entitle the SL to a reduced corporate rate or credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile applicable withholdings and Modelo 202 payments against the annual liability and determine the balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain Spanish payment and withholding certificates and distinguish the SL's corporate liability from withholding tax on later payments to its non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete applicable related-party, tax-incentive, and other supplementary disclosures, and retain supporting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border related-party transactions and relevant non-resident counterparties where required; assess separate transfer-pricing documentation and reporting obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without a payment due can trigger fixed or percentage surcharges under the General Tax Law, depending on whether the taxpayer files voluntarily and the delay; an assessment by the tax authority can instead attract tax penalties. Late payment generally attracts surcharges of 1% plus an additional 1% for each full month of delay during the initial period, followed by a 15% surcharge after 12 months and late-payment interest. False or omitted tax data may attract penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount, depending on the infringement and circumstances. Exact treatment depends on the facts and current statutory provisions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish domestic withholding tax generally applies to dividends paid to non-residents, subject to exemptions, domestic rules, and an applicable tax treaty. A qualifying EU parent company may obtain an exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary regime, generally requiring at least a 10% direct holding and satisfaction of holding-period, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, and other statutory conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the payer with a valid certificate of tax residence issued by the competent foreign tax authority, together with ownership, beneficial-ownership, and treaty-entitlement evidence reasonably required by the payer. The Spanish payer applies a reduced treaty rate or exemption only where statutory conditions are met and must make the applicable withholding and reporting filings. If full domestic withholding is made, the recipient may claim a refund from the AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure and supporting residence and payment evidence. Treaty rates vary by treaty and income category.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The general Spanish non-resident withholding rate is generally 19% for qualifying EU/EEA residents and 24% for other non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and treaty relief. Interest and royalties may qualify for an exemption under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive where all conditions are met, including qualifying associated-company and beneficial-owner requirements. Treaty rates vary by treaty, recipient, and income classification; confirm the applicable treaty and domestic rules before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spanish related-party transactions generally require arm's-length pricing and supporting documentation. Documentation exemptions can apply, including where the aggregate consideration for transactions with the same related person does not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's length during the tax period, subject to exclusions. Simplified local documentation may be available to qualifying groups with net turnover below EUR 45 million. The master file is generally not required for groups below EUR 45 million net turnover, subject to statutory exceptions. These are not universal safe harbours from the arm's-length obligation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not have a general UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation regime. Spanish tax rules nevertheless require genuine commercial substance where relevant, and apply transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, controlled-foreign-company, permanent-establishment, and business-purpose rules. A remittance operator must separately assess Banco de España authorisation and payment-services regulatory requirements; a corporate tax filing does not replace a required financial-services licence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing payment services or executing money remittances in Spain without the authorisation or registration required under Spanish payment-services law, or operating outside the authorised scope.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory sanctions can include substantial fines, cessation orders, and other measures under applicable Spanish payment-services legislation. The precise classification and penalty depend on the conduct, scale, and statutory provision; authorisation should be confirmed with the Banco de España before launch.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may face administrative or criminal exposure where they knowingly participate in unlawful activity or breach duties. Personal liability is not automatic; veil piercing, travel restrictions, and imprisonment require specific legal grounds and process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and terrorist-financing control failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, identify beneficial owners, monitor or report suspicious transactions, maintain required records, or comply with applicable AML controls for a remittance business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish AML legislation provides significant administrative fines and ancillary sanctions, including potential restrictions on activity or management, depending on the breach and responsible party. Criminal liability may arise for money laundering or related offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur personal administrative or criminal liability where statutory responsibility, knowledge, participation, or culpable failure is established. Imprisonment and asset measures require the applicable criminal-law basis and judicial process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion, concealment, or fraudulent returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing taxable income, claiming fictitious deductions, falsifying records, or using sham transactions to evade Spanish tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties generally depend on the infringement and can range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, in addition to tax, interest, and applicable surcharges. Tax fraud meeting the Criminal Code thresholds and elements may result in criminal fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where they personally commit, induce, or knowingly participate in an offence, or where statutory tax-liability derivation rules apply. Imprisonment is a criminal-court sanction; it is not an automatic consequence of a corporate assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party funding, services, intellectual property, or other transactions outside the arm's-length principle; failing to provide required documentation; or using unsupported allocations to shift profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may adjust the taxable base, assess tax and interest, and impose documentation or tax-adjustment penalties under Spanish law. Penalties depend on the adjustment, omissions, and whether the required documentation was available and compliant.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability is not automatic. It may arise under applicable tax-liability, administrative, or criminal rules if the director's own conduct satisfies the required legal elements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend or other payment withholding failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a treaty rate or exemption without adequate residence, beneficial-ownership, holding-period, or eligibility evidence; or failing to withhold, report, and remit tax when required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish payer may be assessed for tax not withheld, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties or surcharges. Treaty relief may be denied where entitlement or anti-abuse conditions are not met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability only where statutory derivation rules or personal administrative or criminal responsibility are established; shareholder non-residence alone does not create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an entity without genuine functions or decision-making to obtain treaty benefits, disguise the beneficial owner, create artificial deductions, or misstate the location of effective management or a permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Authorities may deny treaty relief or deductions, recharacterise transactions, assess tax and interest, and impose applicable penalties. Criminal sanctions require conduct meeting the relevant criminal-law elements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for their own fraudulent participation or under applicable statutory liability provisions. Piercing the corporate veil is exceptional and requires a legal basis and proof.
